hypothesis: A function-0x17 or other address-less/unsupported request can cause modbus_reply to read two bytes beyond the received request because it unconditionally decodes an address before inspecting the function and never verifies req_length.
evidence_source: After only checking ctx, modbus_reply executes address = (req[offset + 1] << 8) + req[offset + 2] at line 724. Address-less functions such as MODBUS_FC_REPORT_SLAVE_ID are parsed by compute_meta_length_after_function with zero metadata, so a received request need only extend through req[offset]. The supplied req_length is not checked before these reads.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: With an exactly sized request buffer, AddressSanitizer reports a heap- or stack-buffer-overflow read at line 724; otherwise the function reads uninitialized bytes beyond the logical request.
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: The same missing request-length validation can expose additional function-specific reads when modbus_reply is called with a truncated request. Validation should occur before every fixed-field or payload access, using req_length after backend framing adjustment.

hypothesis: A write-and-read-registers request whose write address is below start_registers, while its read range is valid, bypasses the range check and writes before tab_registers.
evidence_source: mapping_address_write is computed as address_write - mb_mapping->start_registers at line 953. The range condition at lines 962-965 checks mapping_address < 0 twice; line 964 should check mapping_address_write < 0. A negative mapping_address_write therefore reaches the write loop, where tab_registers[i] is assigned at line 980 with a negative i.
